label: Panna cotta
note: The name is not found in Italian cookbooks before the 1960s, though Piedmont lists it as a traditional food (2001). Some say the older Piedmontese version was set with egg white; others that it descends from French bavarois.

about.text: An Italian dessert of sweetened cream, sometimes with milk, set with gelatin in a mould, flavoured with vanilla, coffee or other things.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Warm cream and sugar are mixed with bloomed gelatin and poured into moulds; it sets on cooling. Too much gelatin makes it rubbery; recipes range from about 3 g to 8 g of gelatin sheet per 500 ml cream.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.name: bloom
steps.note: Gelatin, bloomed in cold water first.
Warmed only until the sugar and gelatin dissolve, not to a boil.
